'''Wolverhampton Wanderers Football Club''' ({{IPAc-en|audio=en-uk-Wolverhampton.ogg|ˌ|w|ʊ|l|v|ər|ˈ|h|æ|m|p|t|ən}} {{respell|WUUL|vər|HAMP|tən}}), commonly referred to as '''Wolves''',<ref name="nickname" /> is a professional [[association football|football]] club based in [[Wolverhampton]], England. The club competes in the [[EFL Championship]], the second tier of [[English football league system|English football]]. The club has played at [[Molineux Stadium]] since moving from [[Dudley Road]] in 1889. The club's traditional kit consists of [[old gold]] shirts and socks with black shorts. Since 1979, the kit has also featured the club's "wolf's head" logo. Long-standing rivalries exist with other clubs from the [[West Midlands (county)|West Midlands]], including [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]], [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]], and [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]], but the main one is the [[Black Country derby]] contested with [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]]. Since 2016, the club has been owned by the Chinese conglomerate [[Fosun International]].

Formed as '''St. Luke's F.C.''' in 1877, the club changed name to Wolverhampton Wanderers two years later and became one of the founding members of the [[English Football League|Football League]] in [[1888–89 Football League|1888]]. They won the [[FA Cup]] for the first time in [[1893 FA Cup Final|1893]], and again as a [[Football League Second Division|Second Division]] team in [[1908 FA Cup Final|1908]] following the club's relegation two years previously. They fell to the third tier in 1923, but went on to win the [[Football League Third Division North|Third Division North]] in 1923–24 and the Second Division in [[1931–32 Football League|1931–32]]. The team was crowned [[List of English football champions|English League champions]] three times – in [[1953–54 Football League|1953–54]], [[1957–58 Football League|1957–58]] and [[1958–59 Football League|1958–59]] – all under the management of [[Stan Cullis]]. Wolves also won another two FA Cup finals, in [[1949 FA Cup Final|1949]] and [[1960 FA Cup Final|1960]]. Relegated in 1965, after 26 consecutive seasons in the top flight, they secured promotion back to the First Division in [[1966–67 Football League|1966–67]]. Wolves won the [[EFL Cup|League Cup]] in [[1974 Football League Cup Final|1974]] and [[1980 Football League Cup Final|1980]], and again won the Second Division title in [[1976–77 Football League|1976–77]].

Wolves suffered a financial crisis during the [[Early 1980s recession|early-1980s recession]] that led to the club coming close to [[liquidation]] in 1982. In the five seasons between [[1981-82 Football League|1981–82]] and [[1985-86 Football League|1985–86]] Wolves were relegated four times (although there was also one promotion in [[1982–83 Football League|1982–83]]), meaning the club ended up in what was then the [[Football League Fourth Division]] (now [[EFL League Two]]) for the first (and so far only) time in the club's history. However, the club immediately started a swift turn-around, and having been beaten in the inaugural Football League play-off final in [[1987 Football League Fourth Division play-off Final|1987]], Wolves won the [[Football League Fourth Division|Fourth Division]] and [[EFL Trophy|Football League Trophy]] titles in [[1987–88 Football League|1987–88]], followed by the [[Football League Third Division|Third Division]] title in [[1988-89 Football League Third Division|1988–89]].

After fourteen seasons in the second tier between 1989 and 2003, Wolves reached the [[Premier League]], founded in 1992, for the first time with victory in the [[2003 Football League First Division play-off Final|2003 play-offs]], though they were relegated after a single season in the top division on this occasion. Wolves won the [[EFL Championship|Championship]] in 2008–09 to return to the Premier League, but endured relegation in [[2011-12 Premier League|2011–12]], followed by relegation again (to [[EFL League One]]) in [[2012-13 Football League Championship|2012–13]]. The club then returned to the Premier League after first winning the [[EFL League One|League One]] title in 2013–14, followed by another Championship title in 2017–18.

After becoming one of the first British clubs to install [[floodlight]]s at its home ground in 1953, Wolves arranged televised "floodlit friendlies" against leading overseas club sides between 1953 and 1956, the most notable being the famous Honved game, which were instrumental in the launch of the [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup]] (now known as the UEFA Champions League) in [[1955–56 European Cup|1955]]. Wolves reached the quarter-finals of the competition in [[1959–60 European Cup|1959–60]] as well as the semi-finals of the [[1960–61 European Cup Winners' Cup]] and the [[1972 UEFA Cup Final|inaugural UEFA Cup Final]] in 1972. Following a 39-year absence from UEFA competitions, they reached the [[2019–20 UEFA Europa League knockout phase#Matches 3|UEFA Europa League finals in 2020]]."}}
